newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares start quietly, brokers meditate.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares start quietly, brokers meditate.

text.p: Singapore shares opened quietly on Thursday with the market in contemplative mood and buyers sidelined awaiting inspiration, dealers said.
"It's a good time to be meditating in the market," said one broker with a local firm.
"Funds are only nibbling and Singapore is seen as more of a regional hedge than a definite buy at the moment," he said.
At 0245 GMT the Straits Times Industrials Index had risen slightly, up 5.06 to 1990.20, with little sign that it would find the strength to break the 2,000 resistance level.
"The market is still on a down trend," another dealer said.
Early traded volume was a muted 25.1 million shares producing 79 gainers to 91 losers.
Lindeteves-Jacoberg was active with more than 1.7 million shares changing hands as the favourable response to its rights issue of loan stocks announced earlier in the week continued.
Blue chip Singapore Press foreign shares topped early gainers up Singapore $0.40 at S$28.40.
Singapore Airlines foreign shares were up S$0.30 at S$12.40 on reports of progress on partnership talks with Ansett Airlines.
